questions.q: What are the three components of every Azure RBAC role assignment?
options: License + group + role definition
Username + password + tenant ID
Security principal + role definition + scope
Resource group + subscription + region
questions.explain: Every Azure permission comes down to who (security principal), what (role definition), and where (scope).

questions.q: What is the key functional difference between the Owner and Contributor built-in roles?
options: Owner can only view resources, never change them
There is no real difference between Owner and Contributor
Contributor can grant access to others, but Owner cannot
Owner can grant access to other people; Contributor can fully manage resources but cannot grant access
questions.explain: Both can fully manage resources, but only Owner can hand out role assignments to other security principals.

questions.q: What can the Reader role do?
options: Nothing at all — Reader is a disabled placeholder role
Grant access to other users, but not create resources
View everything at the assigned scope, but change nothing
Create and delete resources, but not grant access
questions.explain: Reader is view-only — it lets someone see resources and their configuration without being able to modify anything.

questions.q: List the four Azure RBAC scope levels from broadest to narrowest.
options: Management group, subscription, resource group, resource
Tenant, management group, resource group, subscription
Subscription, management group, resource, resource group
Resource, resource group, subscription, management group
questions.explain: A role assigned at a higher scope is inherited by everything beneath it, from management group down to an individual resource.

questions.q: According to the principle of least privilege, what's the correct way to let Alex manage only the VMs in the finance app's resource group?
options: Assign Owner at the subscription level so there's never a permissions issue
Give Alex the tenant's Global Administrator role
Assign Contributor at the scope of that one resource group, not Owner at the subscription
Assign Reader at the management group level
questions.explain: Least privilege means the narrowest role at the narrowest scope that still does the job — Contributor scoped to that one resource group, not a broader grant.
